title: The Sunny morning in May
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：sunny　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sunny 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the clerk wrote of ① a sunny morning in May in the file, and everybody in the office said at once that it was ② sunnier than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the clerk, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the sunny ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the sunniest morning in May anybody in the office had ever seen, or so the file for May 1945 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sunny to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the applicant who had come to help; the sunny ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the stamp at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sunny room on the south side, and said that no applicant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sunny as the room on the south side they had once had in the old office. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sunny or not, and he said so.

By 1958 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the file. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sunny, and nothing besides. The applicant from the next office called the whole plan ⑧ quite sunny; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the file kept the names of the sunny ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1961, before dawn, she wrote of another sunny morning in May in the same file, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ sunnier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The sunniest room on the south side in the whole office, she said in 1963, was the one she could never quite name; the sunny ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 晴朗（前置定语 a sunny morning in May：1951 年书记员在卷宗里记下的那件晴朗的早晨）
B. adj. 晴朗／向阳（比较级 sunnier than：文中两处，一处比五月里晴朗的早晨，一处比预想）
C. adj. 晴朗／向阳（最高级 the sunniest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 晴朗（表语 too sunny to do：母亲觉得它太晴朗，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 向阳（前置定语 a sunny room on the south side：叔叔把整件事称作一桩向阳的房间）
F. adj. 向阳（同级比较 as sunny as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩朝南向阳的房间相比）
G. adj. 向阳（后置定语 something sunny：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 向阳（受程度副词修饰 quite sunny：那位申请人的评价）

items.q: the sunniest morning in May anybody
a sunny room on the south side
The sunniest room on the south side in

answers.why: sunny 意为“晴朗”，1951 年书记员在卷宗里记下的是“一件晴朗的早晨”，此处作前置定语 a sunny morning in May。
sunny 意为“晴朗”，此处用比较级 sunnier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
sunny 意为“晴朗”，卷宗上 五月 那行字说它是办事处里最晴朗的一件，故用最高级 the sunniest morning in May。
sunny 意为“晴朗”，母亲认为这件东西“太晴朗了，谁也用不上”，too sunny to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sunny 意为“向阳”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩向阳的房间”，此处作前置定语 a sunny room on the south side。
sunny 意为“向阳”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩朝南向阳的房间一样向阳”，同级比较用 as sunny as。
sunny 意为“向阳”，卷宗上那半行字要的是“向阳的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sunny。
sunny 意为“向阳”，邻办事处来的那位申请人认为这套计划“相当向阳”，quite 修饰原级 sunny。
sunny 意为“向阳”，1961 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要向阳”，故用比较级 sunnier than。
sunny 意为“向阳”，母亲 1963 年说的是“整个办事处里最向阳的那一桩”，故用最高级 the sunniest room on the south side。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1951 年，书记员在卷宗里记下了一件晴朗的早晨。（a sunny morning in May）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更晴朗。（sunnier than …）
母亲觉得它太晴朗，谁也用不上。（too sunny to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩向阳的房间。（a sunny room on the south side）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩朝南向阳的房间一样向阳。（as sunny as …）
到了 1958 年，卷宗上只剩半行字：要的是一件向阳的东西。（something sunny）
answers: In 1951 the clerk wrote of a sunny morning in May in the file.
Everybody said it was sunnier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too sunny to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sunny room on the south side.
He said nobody would call it as sunny as the room on the south side they had once had.
By 1958 the file asked for nothing but something sunny.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sunny 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1951 the clerk wrote of a sunny morning in May in the file, and nobody forgot it.
It was the sunniest morning in May in the office, or so the file says.
My mother thought it too sunny to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sunny room on the south side, and nobody argued with him.
The applicant from the next office called the plan quite sunny, and everybody laughed.
The sunny ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
